en.title: ZipRecruiter OA #14: Consecutive Triplets of Distinct Characters
en.description: Given a string s containing only lowercase English letters, count the consecutive triplets in s made of pairwise distinct characters. In other words, count the indices i for which s[i], s[i+1], s[i+2] are pairwise different.
en.input: One line with the string s. 1≤length of s≤1000, containing only lowercase English letters.
en.explanation:
Example 1: s="abcdaaae"; i=0 (abc), i=1 (bcd), and i=2 (cda) qualify; in i=3 (daa), s[4] and s[5] are the same, and all later triplets also contain repeated characters, so the answer is 3.
Example 2: s="abacaba"; only i=1 (bac) and i=3 (cab) qualify, and every other triplet contains two a's, so the answer is 2.
Example 3: s="xyz" has only one triplet, which qualifies, so the answer is 1.
hints: You only need to check every window of length 3.
Three characters being pairwise distinct requires comparing three pairs; do not forget the first and last characters.
